statement: The table shows some values of $x$ and $f(x)$ for a linear function $f$. $$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} x & -3 & 1 & 6 & k \\ \hline f(x) & 20 & 8 & -7 & -25 \end{array}$$ What is the value of $k$?

choices.misconception: I found a slope of size $3$ but made it positive, so I used $f(x) = 3x + 5$ and solved $3k + 5 = -25$.
I found the slope $-3$ but used $f(1) = 8$ as if it were the $y$-intercept, so I solved $-3k + 8 = -25$.
I found the slope $-3$ but used the first output, $20$, as the $y$-intercept, so I solved $-3k + 20 = -25$.

hints: Find how much $f(x)$ changes when $x$ goes up by $1$.
Use two columns to find the slope, write the function, then solve $f(k) = -25$.

solutions.elegant: From $x = 6$ to $x = k$ the output falls from $-7$ to $-25$, a drop of $18$. At $3$ per unit that is $6$ units, so $k = 6 + 6 = 12$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
